gloss: just in case; by any chance

definitions.gloss: just in case, by any chance
definitions.explanation: Used to express a very unlikely but possible scenario. Literally "one in ten thousand." Often paired with conditional forms (〜たら、〜ば) or the expression の{場合|ばあい}は to describe precautionary measures or worst-case scenarios.

examples.japanese: {万|まん}が{一|いち}に{備|そな}える。
{万|まん}が{一|いち}のために{保険|ほけん}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: I got insurance just in case.

examples.japanese: {万|まん}が{一|いち}{火事|かじ}が{起|お}きたら、この{非常口|ひじょうぐち}から{逃|に}げてください。
examples.english: In the unlikely event of a fire, please escape through this emergency exit.

notes:
{万|まん}が{一|いち} literally means "one in ten thousand" and is used to talk about unlikely but possible events. It is more emphatic than もしも and carries a stronger sense of improbability.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {万|まん}が{一|いち}に{備|そな}える (prepare for the worst)
- {万|まん}が{一|いち}のために (just in case)
- {万|まん}が{一|いち}の{場合|ばあい} (in the unlikely event)
- {万|まん}が{一|いち}の{事態|じたい} (worst-case scenario)

USAGE:
- Typically used with conditional patterns: {万|まん}が{一|いち}〜たら / 〜ば
- Often appears in formal warnings, safety instructions, and insurance contexts
- Can function as a noun when followed by の: {万|まん}が{一|いち}の{時|とき}
